rules.name: Sensitive access followed by egress
rules.attack_note: T1700 is attached because the actor is an AI agent; T1567.004 replaces T1567 when the host is a known webhook/paste service.
rules.description: A credential store or key file was targeted, then within the window the same session (or its subagent) reached an external destination. The classic exfiltration shape.
rules.false_positives: Legitimate deploys: reading ~/.aws/credentials then calling AWS; git push after touching .env. Allow-list the hosts you deploy to, or the paths your workflow reads.

rules.name: Untrusted content followed by sensitive action
rules.attack_note: Attached to the *downstream* action, not to the fetch: reading a web page is not an attack.
rules.description: Content from outside the trust boundary (a web page, search result, browser page or downloaded file) entered the context, and within the window the agent targeted a credential store, reached a new destination, changed its own configuration or scheduled a job. The indirect prompt-injection shape.
rules.false_positives: Research tasks that fetch docs and then edit config on purpose. The finding is medium when the downstream action is only a new destination, high when it is credential access or a governance change.

rules.name: Credential discovery
rules.attack_note: Refined per store: T1552.004 for private keys, T1555.001 for the macOS keychain, T1555.003 for browser stores.
rules.description: A tool call or command targeted a credential store: SSH keys, cloud credentials, .env files, keychains, browser logins, token-fetching CLIs.
rules.false_positives: Developers ask agents to fix their .env and ssh config. Severity is low for a single read with no follow-on; SL-001 and SL-002 cover the follow-on.

rules.name: First-seen destination near sensitive activity
rules.description: The session reached a host this profile has never contacted before, within the window of a credential access, a config change or an untrusted fetch.
rules.false_positives: The first day on a new project is all first-seen hosts. Seed the baseline by running normally for a while; allow-list your SaaS.

rules.name: Scheduled job or persistence created
rules.attack_note: T1053.003 (Cron) when the mechanism is crontab or a Hermes cron job.
rules.description: A Hermes cron job was created or changed, or a shell command installed OS-level persistence (crontab, launchctl, systemd, schtasks).
rules.false_positives: Users ask for scheduled jobs. The finding is low when the user turn is the direct parent; high when the session was tainted.

rules.name: Plugin or skill set changed
rules.attack_note: No exact ATT&CK technique: extending an agent's own toolset is closest to T1195 (Supply Chain Compromise) only when the source is untrusted, which this rule cannot see.
rules.description: A plugin was installed, enabled, disabled or removed, or a skill was created/installed — the agent changing its own capabilities.
rules.false_positives: Deliberate `hermes plugins install`. Low unless the session was tainted or the change came from a subagent.

rules.name: Approval anomaly
rules.attack_note: Behavioural, not a technique: a denied agent that keeps trying is the signal.
rules.description: Repeated denials, an approval burst, or a tool call that retried the same approval pattern right after a denial.
rules.false_positives: A user denying several unrelated prompts in a row. Threshold is configurable (approval_denies, approval_burst).

rules.name: Subagent acted outside its parent's scope
rules.attack_note: Delegation itself is not a technique; the finding carries the child's action's mapping via SL-001/003.
rules.description: A delegated child session accessed credentials, reached an external host or changed configuration when its parent had done none of those in the window.
rules.false_positives: A parent that delegates 'deploy this' to a child that then legitimately reads credentials. Allow-list paths/hosts for that workflow.

rules.name: Suspicious command shape
rules.attack_note: T1105 for download-and-execute; T1140 for decode-and-run; T1070.003 and T1690 for history tampering; shell rc edits are SL-010.
rules.description: Encoded or downloaded content piped to an interpreter, reverse-shell constructs, hex obfuscation, setuid bits, log or history tampering.
rules.false_positives: Installer one-liners (`curl … | sh`) are common and dangerous in equal measure; the finding says which shape fired.

rules.name: Security configuration or instruction file changed
rules.attack_note: T1685 (Defense Impairment; T1562.001 is revoked in ATT&CK 20) for Hermes config and hooks; T1685.007 when approvals are weakened; T1546.004 for shell rc files; T1098.004 for the SSH authorized-keys file.
rules.description: Hermes config/.env/hooks/plugins, approval mode, agent instruction files (SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md), shell rc files, the SSH authorized-keys file or OS persistence dirs were written.
rules.false_positives: The user editing their own config through the agent. Approval-mode changes are always reported.

rules.name: Code published after sensitive access
rules.attack_note: T1567.001 Exfiltration to Code Repository; secret-in-repo leaks are the common case.
rules.description: git push, a remote change, or a GitHub CLI publish happened in a session that had touched a credential store or a .env file.
rules.false_positives: Normal development after editing .env.example. Allow-list .env.example / templates.

rules.name: Data sent to a webhook or paste service
rules.description: A request to a webhook, tunnel, paste or OOB-interaction service (Discord/Slack webhooks, webhook.site, ngrok, pastebin, interact.sh …).
rules.false_positives: Teams that notify Slack from scripts. Allow-list your own webhook host; the finding is high only when sensitive access preceded it (then SL-001 fires too).

rules.name: Message or delegation after sensitive access
rules.attack_note: A chat platform the agent already talks on is its existing channel; T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel) is the nearest fit and is marked approximate.
rules.description: A send_message / kanban comment, or a subagent spawn, followed a credential access: data moving between agents or out through a chat channel.
rules.false_positives: Status updates to the owner after a deploy. Low unless the message is large or goes to a channel the session had not used.

rules.name: Access to Hermes's own secrets or another profile
rules.description: The agent read or wrote under HERMES_HOME's secret files (.env, auth.json) or another profile's directory.
rules.false_positives: The owner debugging their own install. Always worth a look.
